nodes.label: Scaling Makes Latent Traits More Recoverable

edges.relation: phantom-transfer lineage in agentic synthetic data

tension_sets.claim_A: Foundational experiments: transfer primarily requires shared or behaviorally matched base/initialization.
tension_sets.claim_B: Phantom Transfer and agentic extensions report transfer across model families/architectures.
tension_sets.resolution: Different data-generation, attack, and agentic regimes. Treat same-base dependence as a boundary condition of the original protocol, not a universal law.

tension_sets.claim_A: ICLR mechanistic work finds small prompt paraphrases often suppress subliminal learning.
tension_sets.claim_B: Phantom Transfer reports full sample paraphrasing can fail as a defense.
tension_sets.resolution: Different hidden-signal constructions have different robustness. Paraphrase sensitivity is itself a phenotype to measure.

tension_sets.claim_A: Foundational Nature paper and agentic papers report misalignment/unsafe-behavior transfer.
tension_sets.claim_B: Independent open-source replication reproduced benign preference transfer but not robust broad misalignment.
tension_sets.resolution: Trait class and teacher strength matter; do not generalize from owl/preference transfer to arbitrary value/misalignment transfer.

io_graph_conclusion: The field supports a family of hidden-trait transmission phenomena rather than one monolithic effect. Protocol, model relatedness, trait class, data modality, paraphrasing, scale, and trajectory structure determine transfer strength.
